clue.text: Ornamental shrub is a frothy variety

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different version of it, so these letters come in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener says a showy bush is a bubbly kind of plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' signals an anagram of IS A FROTHY, nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a garden bush grown for its bright yellow spring blossom, so it is an ornamental shrub.

clue.text: Lost youth went off line

definitions.meaning: describes someone whose youthful bloom has gone, like a beauty past her best
describes a signal or line that weakened and disappeared

explanation.surface: A youngster who went missing has dropped off the network.
explanation.definitionFit: Faded means having lost freshness or vigour, and also having died away gradually like a signal.

clue.text: Rescues an artist entangled in a hedge

indicators.note: tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter caught in a hedgerow is freed by rescuers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a protective safeguard against loss, which reassurance offers in the sense of comfort or security.

clue.text: Longed for the old composer to conduct at the centre

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

indicators.note: takes the middle letter of the word conduct

explanation.surface: Someone wished for the elderly composer to lead an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: CONDUCT has seven letters, so its centre is the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something intensely.

clue.text: Paying no attention in Leeds, she got knocked down

indicators.note: being knocked over leaves things in disarray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless woman in a Yorkshire city was hit by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire; its letters with SHE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means taking no notice or heed, careless.

clue.text: Included with stamen, tall flowering spikes

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words stamen and tall

explanation.surface: Botany: tall flower spikes come with stamens.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenta is the plural of amentum, a catkin, which is a hanging spike of flowers.

clue.text: Scorn food

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at what is on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock or jeer, and in British slang scoff is also food or a meal.

clue.text: Italian woman with sex appeal cut by virtual disregard

indicators.note: the sex-appeal letters are split open by the other word
almost the whole thing, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to ignore is to disregard

explanation.surface: An attractive Italian lady is all but snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtual' means almost, so the disregard word loses its last letter before it splits the sex-appeal letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, like Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Small coins offer store of value

definitions.meaning: Scandinavian coins worth a hundredth of a krona or krone
a mineral deposit from which precious metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Loose change provides a way of holding wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is the Swedish and Danish small coin, and ore is also rock holding valuable metal.

clue.text: Strange book, one's that's found up one's sleeve

parts.note: funny means odd or strange
one is, so the word one

explanation.surface: An odd volume is the sort of trick a conjuror keeps up a sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hidden card trick, but the elbow is literally inside the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: The funny bone is the spot at the elbow where a nerve runs, and the elbow sits within the sleeve.

clue.text: Drop a stage play

parts.note: a dram is a small drop of spirits

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon a theatrical production.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for performance on the stage.

clue.text: Laurel, for example, is always envious

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
green with envy, so green means envious

explanation.surface: Someone named Laurel is forever jealous of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel looks like a person's name, but it is the bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurel keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of an evergreen plant.

clue.text: Sort of economic policy that'll stop the balloon going up?

definitions.text: Sort of economic policy that'll stop the balloon going up?

parts.words: Sort of economic policy that'll stop the balloon going up?
parts.note: read literally, a policy that prevents a balloon being blown up; economically, one that keeps prices from rising

explanation.surface: A question about which economic measure keeps prices from ballooning.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy reducing the rate of price rises is said to counter inflation, and a balloon rises by being inflated.

clue.text: Creeping shrub producing a drab rose —- an aberration

indicators.note: a departure from the normal state, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's dull rose has spawned a freak spreading bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aberration' scrambles A DRAB ROSE with AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's beard is a common name for rose of Sharon, a spreading ground-cover St John's wort.

clue.text: Happiness within reach of Kensal Green, said Chesterton

definitions.text: within reach of Kensal Green, said Chesterton
definitions.meaning: G. K. Chesterton's poem The Rolling English Road ends that we shall go to heaven by way of Kensal Green, a London cemetery

explanation.surface: Chesterton remarked that bliss lies close to a district of north-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensal Green is a district of London with a large cemetery, which is why Chesterton's line has the road to heaven pass that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise means a state of perfect bliss, and also the heaven of Chesterton's poem.

clue.text: Falsehoods from each of dozens of people?

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
a jury has twelve members, so juries are groups of a dozen people

explanation.surface: Lies told by every one of a crowd of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Juries of twelve make the 'dozens'; the perjuries are the lies a jury may hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjuries are lies told under oath, so they are falsehoods.

clue.text: Musical function requiring capital arrangement

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A stage show and a social event both need organising in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means of the head here, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle is the way hair on the head (Latin caput) is arranged.

clue.text: A stranger in the streets points that stick out

indicators.note: the stranger word goes inside the abbreviated streets

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, so STS for streets
an alien is a stranger or foreigner

explanation.surface: An unknown figure in town points at something protruding.
explanation.definitionFit: Salients are projecting parts, especially bulges in a battle line that jut into enemy territory.

clue.text: Run joint and cause annoyance

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: Jogging hurts a joint and makes you irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to keep irritating someone or to cause lasting annoyance.

clue.text: Fortifying round the king, being without

indicators.note: the fortifying word goes round the letter for king

parts.note: lacing a drink is fortifying it with spirits
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Defending the monarch while short of supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fortifying' looks military, but it is the lacing of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lacking something is to be without it.

clue.text: The average cavalryman's brief, particular way of speaking

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a lancer is a cavalry soldier armed with a lance

explanation.surface: A typical horse soldier's short instructions are delivered in a special idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a manner of speech or jargon, as in 'legal parlance'.

clue.text: Mark time in descent

parts.note: a line is a mark drawn or made
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Record the passing years in a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, one's line of descent from forebears.

clue.text: Damages for pillage

definitions.meaning: harms or ruins, as a verb

explanation.surface: Compensation is sought for looting.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils means harms or ruins, and spoils are also goods seized by force.

clue.text: Bar in students' club has qualified as entirely satisfactory

indicators.note: the bar word sits inside the students' club word

parts.note: a university students' union is their club
bar means except, as in 'all bar one'
able means competent or qualified

explanation.surface: A drinking spot in the student union has earned a clean bill of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub counter, but it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond objection or criticism is wholly satisfactory.

clue.text: Husbandless woman radical

indicators.note: lacking husband, so H, the abbreviation for husband, is removed

parts.note: Hester is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A single woman with extreme views.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemist's sense of radical is a group of atoms; an ester is such an organic compound group.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an ester is a compound formed from an acid and an alcohol, in older usage a radical-based compound.

clue.text: Sixth sense shows up in teaching

parts.note: tuition is instruction or teaching

explanation.surface: Extrasensory perception turns up in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is knowing without reasoning, popularly called a sixth sense.

clue.text: Drink a peg, say

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken, not written

parts.note: a golf tee is a small peg holding the ball

explanation.surface: A drink, perhaps a short one of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peg' looks like a measure of spirits, but it is the golfer's tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the classic British hot drink.

clue.text: Expect a street singer

parts.note: the waits were bands of carol singers going round the streets at Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates a busker.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the waits were old-style Christmas street musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it, expecting it to come.

clue.text: Confessed about initially lapsing into jargon

indicators.note: the word for confessed goes around the other letter

parts.note: to sing is ... for confessing to the police, so sang means confessed

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone owned up to drifting into technical language.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary, close in sense to the jargon of a group.

clue.text: It upholds a wastrel going round America

indicators.note: the wastrel word goes round the abbreviation for America

parts.note: a spender is one who squanders money
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A good-for-nothing travelling around the United States still keeps something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a strap that holds up a stocking or sock.
